Modern.brandNameRationale: HMS Beagle (1831–36) carried Darwin and his field journals — the notebook as instrument of observation, the small calf-bound book carried in a coat pocket through the Galápagos. Beagle places the brand in the field-journal tradition with the most famous example as the anchor.
Modern.industrySummary: Pocket notebooks have been dominated by a handful of incumbents with reliable shelves at every stationer. There is room for a modern brand that takes the field-journal tradition seriously — house rulings for sketching, specimen notes, and dated observations.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Leuchtturm1917 (leuchtturm1917.com) holds the modern pocket-notebook reference. Baron Fig (baronfig.com) plays the design-led peer position. Rite in the Rain (riteintherain.com) sits in the field-use middle. We sit closer to Baron Fig in posture, sharper on the field-journal framing.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern pocket-notebook brand named for the most famous field journal in science.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 50. Carries a notebook in a coat pocket. Sketches, lists, dates entries. Knows the difference between dot grid and Seyès ruling.
behaviors: Buys notebooks in packs of three
Writes the date at the top of every page

dos: Print the page count and paper weight

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark. Beagle Notebooks set in a calm modern serif, with a single small ship-silhouette hallmark, used on the back cover and the website.

typography.primary: GT Sectra for the wordmark and the back cover
typography.rationale: Sectra carries the field-journal register. Söhne handles the cart.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Vergé (laid) paper is the chain-and-laid line pattern of mould-made paper used in fine European correspondence since the 16th century, distinct from machine-smooth wove paper. Maison + the paper type places the brand in the French papetier tradition. Vergé is a paper-type term, not an active mark.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury correspondence has been moving toward digital invitation suites. There is room for a house that holds the line on laid and watermarked papers, monogrammed and engraved by hand.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Pineider (pineider.com) holds the Italian heritage reference. Le Papier (lepapier.fr) plays the French luxury peer. Mrs. John L. Strong (mrsstrong.com) sits in the New York fine-paper middle. We sit smaller and more French in posture.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A luxury correspondence and engraving house specializing in laid papers.

targetAudience.primary: 40 to 75. Sends handwritten letters. Engages a stationer for the family monogram. Has a paper preference.
behaviors: Sends paper invitations for every occasion

dos: Name the paper, the watermark, the weight
Quote in French where it earns its place
Send paper sample books by post

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark. Maison Vergé set in a high-contrast classical face, with a small hand-drawn watermark hallmark, used in blind emboss on each sheet.

typography.primary: Caslon for the wordmark and printed material
typography.secondary: An engraver's italic for the monogram
typography.rationale: Caslon carries the French papetier register. The engraver's italic handles the monogram.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Iron-gall ink — the medieval-through-19th-century ink (oak galls + iron sulphate + gum arabic) used in the Magna Carta, Bach's manuscripts, and the US Constitution; the ink that defined Western writing for a millennium. The brand is the formula.
Minimal.industrySummary: Ink and pen brands have been multiplying SKUs and seasonal colors. There is room for a minimal house that revives a single iron-gall formula and pairs it with one dip pen.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most minimal ink brands fail this purity test. KWZ Ink (kwzink.com) plays the small-batch ink peer. Rohrer & Klingner (rohrer-klingner.de) sits in the heritage formula middle. We sit further out — one ink, one pen.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A revived iron-gall ink in one bottle, with one matched dip pen.

targetAudience.primary: Adults who write by hand. They want one ink that lasts.

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. Iron Gall in a single-weight grotesk, all lowercase. The favicon is a single small bottle silhouette.

typography.rationale: One face. One ink. One pen.

Corporate.tagline: Cotton bond. Legal sheets. Archive boxes.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Bond paper (originally the paper used for government bonds and stock certificates, cotton-content for durability) and foolscap (the historical legal sheet, 17th c. England). The pair reads as a serious B2B stationer already on the panel at law firms and government offices.
Corporate.industrySummary: B2B stationery has been losing ground to digital documents. There is space for a corporate stationer for legal and financial offices — cotton-bond letterhead, foolscap-sized memo pads, archive boxes.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Crane & Co. (crane.com) holds the institutional cotton-bond reference. Levenger (levenger.com) plays the office-paper peer. Boorum & Pease (now Esselte) sits in the archive-box middle. We sit smaller, focused on legal and financial offices.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A B2B stationer for legal and financial offices.

targetAudience.primary: Law firm office managers, family office administrators, and government procurement officers managing annual stationery spend of $25k to $500k.

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark to the left. The mark is a single foolscap rectangle reduced to two strokes. Reads cleanly on an invoice, a delivery carton, and an email signature.

typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed catalogs and the trade pricing schedule
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean. The serif handles the printed trade catalog.

Creative.brandNameRationale: The Case Study House program (Arts & Architecture magazine, 1945–1966) commissioned the experimental modernist houses — Eames House (#8), Koenig's Stahl House (#22), Neutra's #20 — that defined Southern California mid-century design. The brand inherits the program's aesthetic without echoing any single architect's mark.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative stationery has been chasing risograph zines and pastel pop. There is room for a brand with a mid-century West Coast aesthetic — bright modernist palettes, grid notebooks, architectural-drawing pads.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Present & Correct (presentandcorrect.com) holds the design-led peer reference. Papier (papier.com) plays the modern stationery middle. Hightide (hightide-online.com) sits in the Japanese minimal middle. We sit closer to Present & Correct, with a tighter mid-century frame.
Creative.positioningStatement: A creative stationer with a mid-century West Coast aesthetic.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 50. Reads design magazines. Owns a Saarinen chair, or wants one. Buys notebooks because they like the cover.
behaviors: Reads the Case Study program history

dos: Name the house, the architect, the year
Print the grid in full color

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark. Case Study Stationers set in a geometric mid-century sans, with a single hand-drawn floor-plan rectangle as the hallmark, used on the back cover and the swatch card.

typography.primary: Neutraface for the wordmark and the covers
typography.rationale: Neutraface carries the mid-century West Coast register. Söhne handles the digital.
